title: The stack
subtitle: One server behind one front door, a few rented pieces beside it, and the laptop where every change starts. Push to main is the deploy.

legend.backend: The apps and the deploy loop
legend.security: The front door and the login
legend.edge-emphasis: A change on its way to production

people.label: People
people.note: The owner and the team. In a browser, one Nextcloud login with a second factor opens every private subdomain; on Signal they talk to the assistant. The public sees only the website at the bare domain.
people.bible: | The owner and the team | a browser, one Nextcloud login

laptop.label: Your laptop
laptop.note: Claude Code running in this repository, with the harness: skills, guards, overlays and the code index. Every change starts here as one conversation; open this box for the loop it follows. Nothing deploys from the laptop.

github.label: GitHub
github.note: Holds `main`, the issues and the Projects board. A push to `main` fires the webhook at `deploy.$DOMAIN/hooks/deploy`. The server posts each commit's `vm/gate`, `vm/build`, `vm/boot` and `vm/deploy` status back to its commit page.
github.bible: | A session | git and `gh` | the repository, issues, the board

caddy.label: Caddy
caddy.note: `caddy`, ports 80 and 443, the only container with public ports. It gets its own Let's Encrypt certificates and asks oauth2-proxy about every request to a private subdomain. **Watch out:** it deletes any `Remote-User` header the browser sent, which is why an app can trust that header.
caddy.bible: Caddy is the only container with public ports.

sso.label: Nextcloud
sso.note: `nextcloud` on `cloud.$DOMAIN` with its Postgres, and `oauth2-proxy` on `auth.$DOMAIN`. Accounts live here: Nextcloud is the identity provider, oauth2-proxy the client. The login cookie lasts 8 hours, the Nextcloud session behind it 7 days. Files and calendar live here too.

website.label: website
website.note: `website`, nginx serving the static files in `apps/website/` at the bare domain, public. It links `/design/index.css`, so an edit to `design/tokens.css` restyles it together with the documents and the dashboards.

notulen.label: notulen
notulen.note: `notulen` on `notulen.$DOMAIN`, behind the login. A phone records in five-second chunks; the server stitches them, stores the audio, transcribes, and Claude writes the minutes, committed to `NOTULEN_TARGET_REPO`. CPU transcription works by default and takes hours for a long meeting.

assistant.label: The assistant
assistant.note: The upstream OpenClaw gateway holds the Signal conversation, and this repository's door (`apps/assistant`) triages alerts, decides what reaches a phone and serves the gateway its tools. `signal-cli` is the Signal account both use. It ships empty: no people, no memory.
assistant.bible: The door is this repository's code, and it decides what reaches a phone.

observability.label: Prometheus
observability.note: Prometheus evaluates its rules every 30 seconds and probes each subdomain over HTTPS; Alertmanager hands a firing group to the alert-relay, and the relay to the assistant. Deadmen run as systemd timers and page straight to Signal when the assistant itself is down. Loopback only: Prometheus on 9090.
observability.bible: which hands it unchanged to the assistant.

deploy.label: auto-deploy
deploy.note: `harness-auto-deploy.timer`, every two minutes, plus the push webhook, runs `infra/auto-deploy/auto-deploy.sh`. It picks one commit, the gate tests it in its own tree, and only the changed services are rebuilt and must boot. Red or amber ships nothing. The eject ships off.

vault.label: The vault
vault.note: One Scaleway Secret Manager secret holding the whole environment, secrets included. `infra/secrets/push-env.sh` writes a new version from the laptop; the server pulls it every deploy cycle into `$HARNESS_ROOT/harness.env`, mode 600. A failed pull keeps the old file.
vault.bible: plus every password and token listed in `config/vault.env.example`.

storage.label: Object storage
storage.note: A Scaleway Object Storage bucket (`S3_BUCKET`) for meeting audio. Notulen uploads the stitched recording before any check that could end the session, so every failed job can be retried. **Watch out:** it keeps billing after the server is deleted.
storage.bible: The audio goes to S3 before any check that could end the session, so every failed job can be retried.

gpu.label: GPU tier
gpu.note: Optional. A Scaleway Kapsule cluster whose GPU pools scale to zero, so a node bills only while it transcribes. Notulen submits a Kubernetes Job; the worker writes its result to the stack's Postgres, which then listens beyond the server with only its password as guard.
gpu.bible: so a node bills only while it transcribes.

slides.label: People reach it two ways: a browser through Caddy, and Signal to the assistant
Caddy is the only public door, and one Nextcloud login opens every private name
Notulen keeps its audio in object storage and can borrow a GPU while it transcribes
Prometheus watches all of it and hands every alert to the assistant
Every change starts on the laptop as a push; the server tests it, pulls the vault and ships
